newsitem.title: EGYPT: Egypt blames Israel for tension with Syria.
newsitem.headline: Egypt blames Israel for tension with Syria.

text.p: Egypt's ambassador to Israel blamed Israelis on Saturday for war talk with Syria and said the Jewish state should not abuse the commitment of Arab states to a peaceful Middle East settlement.

Ambassador Mohammed Bassiouny, who was summoned to the Israeli foreign ministry on Friday over Egyptian press attacks on Israeli leaders, was speaking to reporters after a three-hour session with Egyptian Foreign Minister Amr Moussa.
"The situation between the two sides (Israel and Syria) flared up and escalated as a result of some statements from Israel which were provocative and incompatible with the spirit of peace," he said.

"If the Arab states took a strategic decision in favour of peace as an option... that does not mean that one party can provoke the other by adopting the method of force and muscle- flexing -- because that is unacceptable," he added.
Bassiouny said the answer was for Israel and Syria to resume negotiations where they left off and on the same basis, including the principle of land for peace.
The ambassador defended the Egyptian press from Israeli criticism but also said he opposed personal attacks.
Egyptian newspapers, many of them state institutions, have repeatedly described Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu as stupid, arrogant and deceitful.
Egyptian President Hosni Mubarak said earlier on Saturday he could not control the Egyptian press but would like it to avoid what he called "base expressions".
Bassiouny said: "The Israeli government expressed to me its displeasure with what has been published in the Egyptian press against the person of the Israeli prime minister.
"We express our opinions objectively about policies but we are not in favour of attacking any person.
"The peace agreement (between Israel and Egypt) does not mean agreeing with everything Israel does but I must express my opinion in a truly democratic and objective way."
Bassiouny is back in Cairo for a visit on Monday by Israeli President Ezer Weizman, seen in Egypt as an elder statesman in contrast with the young and less experienced Netanyahu.

"He is one of the founders of the Camp David agreements (between Israel and Egypt in 1978) and one of the founders of Egyptian-Israeli relations, which he works constantly to promote and develop," the ambassador said.
